basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 18.' and it opens '(Cap. IX.—Vers. 18.) Et erant filii Noe, qui egressi sunt de arca, Sem, Cham, et Japheth.'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. IX.—Vers. 18.) Et erant filii Noe, qui egressi sunt de arca, Sem, Cham, et Japheth. Frequenter Septuaginta Interpretes non valentes HETH (ח) litteram, quae duplicem aspirationem sonat, in Graecum sermonem vertere, chi (χ) Graecam litteram addiderunt: ut nos docerent in istiusmodi vocabulis aspirare debere: unde et in praesenti loco, Cham transtulerunt, pro eo quod est HAM, a quo et Aegyptus usque hodie Aegyptiorum lingua HAM dicitur.
